findings.claim: reviewScratch creates the reviewer's folder at a fixed, predictable path, FileManager.temporaryDirectory/collie-review/<name>-<8hex>, with withIntermediateDirectories. That parent is the user's DARWIN_USER_TEMP_DIR, which the judged agent's strict sandbox can write (SandboxProfile.swift:166 allows sub(real(i.userTemp))). During its turn the agent can plant $TMPDIR/collie-review/CLAUDE.md (or $TMPDIR/CLAUDE.md), and Claude Code loads every ancestor CLAUDE.md of the cwd. It can also make collie-review a symlink into the worktree or a folder it controls, which createDirectory follows and realPath resolves. Either way every reviewer loads instructions the agent wrote, and the prompt hands them the nonce, so the central anti-goal falls again. The X1 test only checks that the cwd itself is empty.
findings.fix: Create the scratch with mkdtemp under a daemon-owned folder that the agents' profile keeps closed to writes (Collie's Application Support, which the sandbox already denies), refuse if any component of the path is a symlink (lstat), and add a test that plants CLAUDE.md in the scratch's parent folders and in a symlinked collie-review and expects the reviewer not to get it, or the review to fail closed.

findings.claim: 'o revisor mexeu na árvore' is recorded as an ordinary review refusal: it sets facts.review and does reviewRejects += 1, so on the agent's next refusal, or right away when reviewRejectsInRow >= 1, the task is deferred as 'recusada duas vezes pela revisão: chame o dono'. The work was never actually judged, and what moved the tree may be the reviewer or a leftover process.
findings.fix: Treat reviewerTouched like reviewBudgetOut (uncount with a note, without touching reviewRejects), or at least do not add it to reviewRejects.

findings.claim: With scratch set, if ensurePaddock (or a throw after launch that is not inside the do/catch with remove) fails after launch succeeded, the defer takes the reviewer out of loopReviewers while its terminal stays alive in ws.terminals. The loop never gets its id, so it never dismisses it, and until the next daemon start (the only isReviewer sweep) loopOthersWorking counts it as 'outro agente trabalhando'.
findings.fix: On that failure, remove the terminal (try? await remove(rec)) before unmarking it, or keep it marked until loopDismiss.

findings.claim: The line count runs one `git show judged:<path>` per changed path, in sequence, with no limit and no budget check, and reads each whole file into memory (binaries included) only to count its lines. This happens after `rest` was measured against reviewMinTurn, so a diff with thousands of files, or big files, holds the attempt and overruns the budget before the reviewers are even summoned.
findings.fix: Cap the number of paths and the bytes read (skip the line check past a limit, or use one `git cat-file --batch` with a size cap), and measure `left` again right before computing the turn.

previous.claim: summonReviewer reused the worker's summon, so the reviewer started in the worktree and loaded the CLAUDE.md, settings and hooks the judged agent committed.
previous.why: The reviewer no longer starts in the worktree, but the new scratch sits in a temp folder the agent can write and reach through symlinks, so the agent can still put a CLAUDE.md where every reviewer loads it (new blocker).

previous.claim: Reviewers were left out of othersWorking without anything enforcing that they do not write, and nothing measured the tree again after the review.
previous.why: reviewTree captures HEAD and `status --porcelain -b` before and after, requires HEAD == judged, and on a difference resets to judged and refuses with 'o revisor mexeu na árvore'.

previous.claim: A cancel in the middle of the review counted mute reviewers as a refusal (reviewRejects+1 and a note) that survived the uncount.
previous.why: `.reviewDone` is now in judges() and `.runReview` returns `.cancelled` before record when Task.isCancelled.

previous.claim: reviewRejects only went back to 0 on an approval, so a reopen, a new run or a check failure in between did not start the count over.
previous.why: It is now reset on reopen (WorkStore), at the start of each run, on a deferral, and on any failure before the review (markOpenOrDeferred with `last || refused == nil`).

previous.claim: With the budget spent, the reviewer's ~1 s turn made every persona mute, and that counted as a refusal.
previous.why: Under reviewMinTurn (20 s) the effect returns `.reviewBudgetOut`, which uncounts the attempt and stops the loop with budgetSpent without touching reviewRejects.

previous.claim: A reviewer was marked in loopReviewers only after its summon returned, so another loop could count it as working while it booted.
previous.why: summon(scratch:) inserts rec.id into loopReviewers before launch, and the defer removes it only on failure (see the new minor about failing after launch).

previous.claim: Reviewers left alive by a daemon that fell mid-review counted as someone working after a restart.
previous.why: loopAgents now includes every terminal of the paddock where AgentNaming.isReviewer holds (the '-rev' suffix plus a 'collie-review' cwd), so the start sweep dismisses it.
